sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhaktatyāgaṃ prāhur atyantapāpaṃ; tulyaṃ loke brahmavadhyākṛtena tasmān nāhaṃ jātu kathaṃ canādya; tyakṣyāmy enaṃ svasukhārthī mahendra
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: They declare the abandonment of one who is devoted to be a most grievous sin, equal in the world to the crime of slaying a brahmin. Therefore, O great Indra, never, in any way, will I today forsake this one for the sake of my own happiness.

sanskrit: indra uvāca śunā dṛṣṭaṃ krodhavaśā haranti; yad dattam iṣṭaṃ vivṛtam atho hutaṃ ca tasmāc chunas tyāgam imaṃ kuruṣva; śunas tyāgāt prāpsyase devalokam
english: Indra said: Whatever is given, offered in sacrifice, set forth openly, or poured into the fire — the Krodhavaśas carry it off if it has been looked upon by a dog. Therefore make this abandonment of the dog; by abandoning the dog you shall attain the world of the gods.

sanskrit: tyaktvā bhrātṝn dayitāṃ cāpi kṛṣṇāṃ; prāpto lokaḥ karmaṇā svena vīra śvānaṃ cainaṃ na tyajase kathaṃ nu; tyāgaṃ kṛtsnaṃ cāsthito muhyase 'dya
english: Having forsaken your brothers and even your beloved Kṛṣṇā, O hero, you have won this world by your own deeds. How then do you not forsake this dog? Established in renunciation entire, why are you bewildered now?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na vidyate saṃdhir athāpi vigraho; mṛtair martyair iti lokeṣu niṣṭhā na te mayā jīvayituṃ hi śakyā; tasmāt tyāgas teṣu kṛto na jīvatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: With mortals who are dead there can be neither alliance nor enmity — such is the settled truth among men in the world. I had no power to bring them back to life; therefore my forsaking of them was the forsaking of the dead, not of the living.

sanskrit: pratipradānaṃ śaraṇāgatasya; striyā vadho brāhmaṇasvāpahāraḥ mitradrohas tāni catvāri śakra; bhaktatyāgaś caiva samo mato me
english: The surrendering back of one who has come for refuge, the slaying of a woman, the seizing of a brahmin's wealth, the betrayal of a friend — these four, O Śakra, and the abandonment of one devoted, I hold to be equal.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tad dharmarājasya vaco niśamya; dharmasvarūpī bhagavān uvāca yudhiṣṭhiraṃ prītiyukto narendraṃ; ślakṣṇair vākyaiḥ saṃstavasaṃprayuktaiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard that speech of the King of Righteousness, the blessed one — Dharma himself in bodily form — spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, lord of men, filled with affection, in gentle words joined with praise.

sanskrit: abhijāto 'si rājendra pitur vṛttena medhayā anukrośena cānena sarvabhūteṣu bhārata
english: You are nobly born, O king of kings, in the conduct of your father and in wisdom, and in this compassion of yours toward all beings, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: purā dvaitavane cāsi mayā putra parīkṣitaḥ pānīyārthe parākrāntā yatra te bhrātaro hatāḥ
english: Once before, in the Dvaita forest, you were tested by me, my son, where your brothers, striving for the sake of water, were struck down.

sanskrit: bhīmārjunau parityajya yatra tvaṃ bhrātarāv ubhau mātroḥ sāmyam abhīpsan vai nakulaṃ jīvam icchasi
english: There, setting aside both your brothers Bhīma and Arjuna, desiring equity between your two mothers, you wished that Nakula should live.

sanskrit: ayaṃ śvā bhakta ity eva tyakto devarathas tvayā tasmāt svarge na te tulyaḥ kaś cid asti narādhipa
english: "This dog is devoted to me" — for this very reason you have refused the celestial chariot. Therefore, O ruler of men, there is none in heaven equal to you.

sanskrit: atas tavākṣayā lokāḥ svaśarīreṇa bhārata prāpto 'si bharataśreṣṭha divyāṃ gatim anuttamām
english: Hence imperishable worlds are yours in your own body, O Bhārata; you have attained, O best of the Bhāratas, a divine and unsurpassed destiny.

sanskrit: tato dharmaś ca śakraś ca marutaś cāśvināv api devā devarṣayaś caiva ratham āropya pāṇḍavam
english: Then Dharma and Śakra, the Maruts too and the Aśvins, the gods and the divine sages, having set the son of Pāṇḍu upon the chariot —

sanskrit: prayayuḥ svair vimānais te siddhāḥ kāmavihāriṇaḥ sarve virajasaḥ puṇyāḥ puṇyavāgbuddhikarmiṇaḥ
english: — set forth in their own celestial cars, those perfected ones who move at will, all free from passion, holy, pure in speech and thought and deed.

sanskrit: sa taṃ rathaṃ samāsthāya rājā kurukulodvahaḥ ūrdhvam ācakrame śīghraṃ tejasāvṛtya rodasī
english: Mounting that chariot, the king who upheld the line of the Kurus rose swiftly upward, enveloping heaven and earth with his splendor.

sanskrit: tato devanikāyastho nāradaḥ sarvalokavit uvācoccais tadā vākyaṃ bṛhadvādī bṛhattapāḥ
english: Then Nārada, knower of all worlds, standing amid the host of the gods, eloquent of speech and mighty in austerity, spoke aloud these words:

sanskrit: ye 'pi rājarṣayaḥ sarve te cāpi samupasthitāḥ kīrtiṃ pracchādya teṣāṃ vai kururājo 'dhitiṣṭhati
english: Even all those royal sages who are gathered here — the king of the Kurus surpasses them, eclipsing their renown.

sanskrit: lokān āvṛtya yaśasā tejasā vṛttasaṃpadā svaśarīreṇa saṃprāptaṃ nānyaṃ śuśruma pāṇḍavāt
english: Having pervaded the worlds with his fame, his splendor, and the richness of his conduct, having come hither in his own body — of none other than the son of Pāṇḍu have we ever heard such a thing.

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā rājā vacanam abravīt devān āmantrya dharmātmā svapakṣāṃś caiva pārthivān
english: Hearing the words of Nārada, the king of righteous soul addressed the gods, and the kings of his own party as well, and spoke this speech:

sanskrit: śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ sthānam adya me tad eva prāptum icchāmi lokān anyān na kāmaye
english: Be it good or be it evil, whatever the abode of my brothers, that alone do I now wish to attain; other worlds I do not desire.

sanskrit: rājñas tu vacanaṃ śrutvā devarājaḥ puraṃdaraḥ ānṛśaṃsyasamāyuktaṃ pratyuvāca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Hearing the king's speech, so full of compassion, the king of the gods, Puraṃdara, replied to Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: sthāne 'smin vasa rājendra karmabhir nirjite śubhaiḥ kiṃ tvaṃ mānuṣyakaṃ sneham adyāpi parikarṣasi
english: Dwell in this abode, O king of kings, won by your auspicious deeds. Why do you still drag along with you this human attachment?

sanskrit: siddhiṃ prāpto 'si paramāṃ yathā nānyaḥ pumān kva cit naiva te bhrātaraḥ sthānaṃ saṃprāptāḥ kurunandana
english: You have attained the supreme perfection, as no other man has ever anywhere attained it. Your brothers have not reached this abode, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: adyāpi mānuṣo bhāvaḥ spṛśate tvāṃ narādhipa svargo 'yaṃ paśya devarṣīn siddhāṃś ca tridivālayān
english: Even now the human condition clings to you, O ruler of men. This is heaven — behold the divine sages and the perfected ones who dwell in the third heaven.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu devendram evaṃvādinam īśvaram punar evābravīd dhīmān idaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: But the wise Yudhiṣṭhira, to the lord Indra of the gods who spoke thus, again spoke these meaningful words:

sanskrit: tair vinā notsahe vastum iha daityanibarhaṇa gantum icchāmi tatrāhaṃ yatra me bhrātaro gatāḥ
english: Without them I have no will to dwell here, O slayer of the Daityas. I wish to go there, to where my brothers have gone,

sanskrit: yatra sā bṛhatī śyāmā buddhisattvaguṇānvitā draupadī yoṣitāṃ śreṣṭhā yatra caiva priyā mama
english: and to where that stately dark-hued lady, endowed with wisdom and goodness and every virtue, Draupadī, best of women, my beloved, has gone.
